planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly in late summer to fall so the top is barely covered, allowing roots to establish before frost.

directions: A plicata-patterned tall bearded iris with pale lobelia-violet and yellow smoky standards above falls that show a straw-yellow center bordered by a wide, velvety port-wine margin. Marigold-orange beards and a lace-edged finish give the late-midseason blooms an intricate, almost woven look. Grow in full sun with sharp drainage and divide congested clumps every three to four years to maintain strong bloom.

planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly in late summer to fall so the top is barely covered, allowing roots to establish before frost.

directions: An early-midseason tall bearded iris with warm brass-gold standards flushed grey-mauve at the center, over falls that shift from dandelion-gold shoulders to clear dandelion yellow. Deep chrome-yellow beards and purple-based foliage add contrast to this glowing, metallic-toned bloom. Thrives in full sun with good drainage and benefits from division every few years once clumps crowd.

planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly in late summer to fall so the top is barely covered, allowing roots to establish before frost.

directions: A heavily ruffled tall bearded iris with orange standards washed in a pink midrib flush, cadmium-orange style arms, and amber-yellow falls rimmed and shouldered in cadmium orange around orange beards. Blooms carry a pronounced sweet fragrance from midseason into late season. Best in full sun with well-drained soil, and divide crowded clumps to keep flowering vigorous.

planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly in late summer to fall so the top is barely covered, allowing roots to establish before frost.

directions: A late to very-late blooming tall bearded iris in warm autumn tones, with salmon standards edged yellow-orange over yellow-orange falls shaded grey-orange at the edges and shoulders. Orange beards and a slight sweet fragrance complete the ruffled, well-branched stalks that carry seven to nine buds. Grow in full sun with sharp drainage, dividing clumps every few years for best bloom.

planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly in late summer to fall so the top is barely covered, allowing roots to establish before frost.

directions: A midseason tall bearded iris in soft true pink on white, with creamy pink standards veined deeper pink at the midribs and a light violet edge on the style arms. The creamy-white falls carry dark pink shoulders and a half-inch pink rim beneath heavy bubble ruffling. Sturdy, thick show stalks carry numerous buds; grow in full sun with good drainage for best performance.

planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly in late summer to fall so the top is barely covered, allowing roots to establish before frost.

directions: A midseason tall bearded iris with russet-and-yellow blended standards finely veined in light red above lavender-mauve falls, each marked with a deep red blaze around an orange beard and short white rays. The bicolor contrast and slight fragrance give it a warm, richly patterned presence in the border. Grow in full sun with well-drained soil and divide every few years to sustain vigorous bloom.
